:::{#exm-weighted-inner-product}
#### A weighted inner product

Let $\vecf{c} = (c_1, \ldots, c_p)$ be a vector of positive numbers, and define

$$\iprod{\vx}{\vy}_{\vecf{c}} \eqdef \sumip c_i\,x_i y_i.$$

This function is also an inner product on $\reals^p$
[@axler2024linear, Example 6.3(b), p. 184]:

- **positivity**: $\iprod{\vx}{\vx}_{\vecf{c}} = \sumip c_i\,x_i^2$,
  and each term $c_i\,x_i^2$ is a positive number times a square, so the sum is at least $0$;
- **definiteness**: a sum of nonnegative terms is $0$ exactly when every term is $0$,
  and $c_i\,x_i^2 = 0$ exactly when $x_i = 0$, because $c_i > 0$;
  so $\iprod{\vx}{\vx}_{\vecf{c}} = 0$ exactly when $\vx = \vzero_{p \times 1}$;
- **linearity in the first slot**: see the derivation after this list;
- **symmetry**: $c_i\,x_i y_i = c_i\,y_i x_i$ for each $i$,
  so $\iprod{\vx}{\vy}_{\vecf{c}} = \iprod{\vy}{\vx}_{\vecf{c}}$.

For linearity in the first slot,
take $\vx, \vy, \vecf{z} \in \reals^p$ and real numbers $a, b$:

$$
\ba
\iprod{a\,\vx + b\,\vy}{\vecf{z}}_{\vecf{c}}
&= \sumip c_i\,(a\,\vx + b\,\vy)_i\,z_i
&& \text{(definition of } \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}_{\vecf{c}} \text{)}
\\
&= \sumip c_i\,(a x_i + b y_i)\,z_i
&& \text{(@def-scalar-mult, @def-vector-addition)}
\\
&= \sumip \paren{a\,c_i x_i z_i + b\,c_i y_i z_i}
&& \text{(distribute, and commute the factors in each product)}
\\
&= \sumip a\,c_i x_i z_i + \sumip b\,c_i y_i z_i
&& \text{(split the finite sum)}
\\
&= a \sumip c_i x_i z_i + b \sumip c_i y_i z_i
&& \text{(factor } a \text{ and } b \text{ out of the sums)}
\\
&= a\,\iprod{\vx}{\vecf{z}}_{\vecf{c}} + b\,\iprod{\vy}{\vecf{z}}_{\vecf{c}}
&& \text{(definition of } \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}_{\vecf{c}} \text{)}
\ea
$$

Different inner products can give different numbers for the same pair of vectors.
With $p = 2$, $\vecf{c} = (2, 1)$, $\vx = (1, 3)$ and $\vy = (4, -1)$:

$$
\ba
\iprod{\vx}{\vy}_{\vecf{c}}
&= 2 \cd 1 \cd 4 + 1 \cd 3 \cd (-1)
&& \text{(definition of } \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}_{\vecf{c}} \text{)}
\\
&= 8 - 3
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= 5
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

while the dot product of the same vectors is

$$
\ba
\vx \cdot \vy
&= 1 \cd 4 + 3 \cd (-1)
&& \text{(definition of the dot product)}
\\
&= 4 - 3
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= 1
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

:::
